key_insight: RATS shows that a vision transformer can learn a compositional, part-based representation on its own by splitting the usual class token into multiple learnable register tokens. These registers help patches communicate through an L→N→N→L pathway, encouraging emergent structure instead of treating the image as a flat whole.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of getting self-supervised vision models to discover reusable object parts and structured representations, rather than only learning global image-level features.
method: Replace the single classification token with N learnable register tokens.
Route patch information through a register-mediated communication pattern: L→N→N→L.
Use this register attention design to encourage emergent part discovery and compositional organization in vision transformers.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical way to improve interpretability and structure in self-supervised vision models. It may lead to representations that transfer better to downstream tasks by capturing reusable parts and object structure more naturally.

paper_title: RATS! Patches Talk Through Registers: Emergent Parts in Register Attention Transformers
